title: Security posture discovery with Solaris Tech
next_steps: Send SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 cert
Share VPC/private deployment network diagram and connector requirements
Schedule Dedicated POC for benchmark (proposed week of 2027-09-27)
action_items: Diego Alvarez: Prepare POC test plan + target latency/cost metrics (due 2027-09-20)
Maya Chen: Send compliance pack (SOC2, ISO) and third-party pen-test summary (due 2027-09-15)

summary: Discovery focused on Solaris Tech's security requirements for evaluating Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private. Key asks: SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML integration path, RBAC and audit log retention, KMS integration for customer-managed keys, data residency and retention controls. Agreement to run a dedicated POC and share compliance artifacts.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-14
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Rajiv Patel (CTO, Solaris), Lina Gomez (Head of Security, Solaris), Marcus Lee (Infra)

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, with Diego our solutions engineer. Quick intro round?
[00:12] Rajiv (Solaris CTO): Hey Rajiv here, CTO. Lina is our security lead, Marcus handles infra.
[00:18] Lina (Solaris Sec): hi all. We're mainly here to understand your security posture for a potential deployment of Redwood - hosted vs dedicated vs private.
[00:28] Diego (Redwood SE): Great, we'll start with a high-level then dig into specifics like SOC2, ISO, SSO, KMS, audit logs. We might ask about your compliance requirements too.
[00:37] Marcus (Solaris Infra): Quick note: our procurement needs to see a SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 evidence, plus network diagrams for private deployments.
[00:47] Maya: Totally. We can share the SOC2 report and ISO certs, plus a redacted pen test summary. I'll send those after.
[00:53] Lina: Good. On SSO we use Okta with SAML and SCIM for provisioning. We need RBAC integration and SCIM user sync.
[01:05] Diego: We support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM for provisioning. Roles map via SCIM groups or we can integrate with your IdP. For Dedicated/Private we support SSO behind customer VPC with SAML assertion to the control plane.
[01:22] Rajiv: For dedicated vs hosted — our main worry is data leakage and logs. If we go hosted, how long does Redwood retain audit logs and customer data? Can we control retention?
[01:34] Maya: Hosted default retention is 90 days for detailed request logs, with longer aggregated metrics. For enterprise customers we offer flexible retention and can adjust to meet retention policies. We also have an option to push logs to customer-managed S3 or Splunk.
[01:49] Lina: Pushing logs is important. Also need assurance that PII isn't used to train any shared models.
[01:56] Diego: We have a no-training policy on customer data for hosted with enterprise contracts, and we can include contractual clauses. For Private deployments there's no data leaving your environment.
[02:12] Marcus: On encryption — we use a KMS in AWS today and want customer-managed keys. Does Redwood support CMKs/HSM?
[02:20] Diego: Yes, we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations and HSM. For Hosted we offer a bring-your-own-key (BYOK) flow with KMS; for Dedicated/Private you can fully manage keys in your cloud or on-prem HSM.
[02:33] Rajiv: Good. Can you explain how keys are used — at rest vs in transit? Is the model shard encrypted?
[02:42] Diego: All persistent storage is encrypted at rest with your CMK if configured. In transit is TLS 1.2/1.3. The runtime keeps KV caches in memory; for long-lived caches we offer optional encrypted storage. We can walk through a detailed KMS diagram in the follow-up doc.
[02:58] Lina: Auditability — who has access to keys and logs at Redwood? We need separation of duties and restricted access for support engineers.
[03:07] Maya: Access is RBAC controlled via our identity system; support access to customer data is gated through Just-In-Time escalation and requires approval/audit. We keep detailed access logs for support sessions.
[03:18] Lina: Do you provide immutable audit logs and retention policies for compliance?
[03:24] Diego: Yes, audit logs are write-once in our system; we also support exporting them to your SIEM. Retention policies are configurable per account.
[03:33] Rajiv: On certifications, can you share the scope of SOC 2 — is it Type II with the security and availability trust service criteria?
[03:41] Maya: It's SOC 2 Type II covering Security and Availability; ISO 27001 scope includes our control plane and hosting services. I'll attach the certs.
[03:49] Lina: We also need to know about vulnerability management and third-party pen tests.
[03:54] Diego: We run quarterly vulnerability scans, annual third-party pentests, and CVE-based patching processes. We'll share high-level reports.
[04:05] Marcus: Network topology for Private — do you support customer VPC peering or do you require a VPN tunnel? Latency is a concern for inference.
[04:15] Diego: For Private deploys we support several connectivity patterns: VPC peering (where supported), AWS PrivateLink, and site-to-site VPN. For low-latency dedicated we typically recommend colocated Dedicated nodes in the same cloud region and VPC peering or PrivateLink.
[04:30] Rajiv: If we want to do a POC, we'd like to test latency and cost for our workload. What's the POC process?
[04:38] Maya: We usually offer a short Dedicated POC where we provision a small GPU pool with reserved capacity. Diego will draft a POC test plan with target SLOs — latency p50/p95, throughput, and cost per 1k tokens.
[04:51] Diego: I'll prepare a test plan. Question for Marcus, what's your typical request size and concurrency?
[04:56] Marcus: Typical request length is 512 tokens, with bursts up to 25 concurrent model streams.
[05:03] Diego: Good — we'll size the POC accordingly.
[05:06] Lina: What about role-based access inside Redwood — can we map internal roles to Redwood roles and enforce least privilege?
[05:14] Diego: Yes, RBAC is flexible. You can map IdP groups to Redwood roles (admin, dev, viewer). We also have API keys with scoped permissions and short TTL tokens.
[05:25] Rajiv: Are there rate-limiting and quota guardrails to prevent accidental overuse?
[05:31] Maya: Yes, per-API-key quotas and rate limits, plus alerting and cost dashboards.
[05:37] Lina: Pen-testing support — if we engage in an internal red team against our test environment will Redwood require coordination?
[05:44] Diego: For hosted, any active security testing requires a coordinated disclosure process; we can set up a safe window for a POC. For Dedicated/Private under an enterprise agreement it's easier since the environment is isolated.
[05:58] Rajiv: Any standard contractual SLAs for uptime and latency?
[06:03] Maya: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; hosted has best-effort + enterprise tiers with availability commitments. We'll include SLA language in the proposal.
[06:13] Marcus: About data residency — we have EU customers; can you guarantee that data stays in region?
[06:19] Maya: Yes, we have region-specific hosting and can restrict routing to EU-only regions for both Hosted (enterprise tenancy) and Dedicated/Private deployments.
[06:28] Lina: Retention specifics again — can we set different retention for transcripts vs metrics vs debug logs?
[06:34] Diego: Yes, retention is tiered. You can set short retention for raw transcripts, longer for aggregated metrics. We can also push raw logs to your storage.
[06:44] Speaker 1: (overlap) excuse me — does Redwood use customer data for model improvements?
[06:49] Maya: We do not use customer data to train public models unless explicitly allowed in the contract. For hosted enterprise accounts we can contractually commit no-training.
[06:58] Lina: Are there any known multi-tenant leakage risks with hosted?
[07:03] Diego: We've invested in strict tenant isolation at the runtime and orchestration layer. For extremely sensitive workloads we recommend Dedicated or Private to remove any shared control plane concerns.
[07:14] Rajiv: Let's talk about secrets management — do you allow injection of secrets into the runtime or do we need to manage them separately?
[07:22] Diego: We support secret references where secrets are stored in your KMS and passed securely at runtime. For Private you manage everything internally.
[07:31] Marcus: Logging of prompts — we need the ability to mask or not persist raw prompts in logs for regulatory reasons. Is that possible?
[07:39] Maya: Yes, masking is available. You can configure to redact PII or not store raw prompts. That's part of the POC config.
[07:48] Lina: For compliance reviews our legal team will want encryption in transit details, key rotation policies, and evidence of staff background checks. Do you have those artifacts?
[07:58] Maya: We'll include a compliance packet with key rotation policy, staff vetting summary, and SOC2 auditor contact info.
[08:07] Rajiv: Any remarks about disaster recovery and backups?
[08:11] Diego: We have cross-region backups for critical control plane metadata and automated snapshotting. For customer data you can opt-in to encrypted cross-region backups or keep it within region.
[08:22] Speaker 2 (unum): (mumble) sorry — how are model updates handled?
[08:26] Diego: Model updates are versioned. You pin model versions and we manage rollouts with canary or A/B. There's an audit trail for model changes.
[08:36] Lina: Who signs the DPA — Redwood or the reseller? We need DPA and security addendum with specific clauses for no-training, breach notification timelines.
[08:46] Maya: Redwood signs the DPA; we have a standard security addendum that covers no-training, 72-hour breach notification, and incident response commitments. We'll share a draft.
[08:58] Rajiv: On the infrastructure side, do you support private endpoints only accessible from our VPC?
[09:04] Diego: Yes, Private and Dedicated support private endpoints; for Hosted enterprise we offer private connectivity options like PrivateLink.
[09:11] Marcus: Monitoring interfaces — do we get per-request tracing to our tracing system?
[09:16] Diego: We expose tracing hooks and can forward traces to your tracing backend; we also include per-request IDs for correlating logs.
[09:26] Lina: Any history of incidents in the last 24 months we should be aware of?
[09:31] Maya: We maintain a public security page with incident summaries; nothing material in the last 12 months, and we'll provide details in the compliance pack.
[09:42] Rajiv: Ok good. On pricing — if we start Dedicated POC and scale to reserved capacity, how does pricing change?
[09:49] Maya: POC is usage-based with a short-term reserved instance for predictability; full Dedicated reserved contracts offer lower unit costs and burst capacity options. We'll include estimated TCO in the proposal.
[10:02] Diego: One operational note — for low-latency inference we recommend enabling prefix KV caching and optimized kernels; we'll include recommended config for your request size.
[10:15] Marcus: That caching — is any customer data persisted in the cache across requests?
[10:20] Diego: Cache entries are ephemeral per-session unless configured for longer-lived caches; we can disable persistent caches for compliance-sensitive workloads.
[10:29] Lina: Can you provide an example of the audit log entries we would receive?
[10:34] Diego: We'll attach a sample audit log: timestamp, user id, action, resource, request id, and optional redacted payload.
[10:41] Rajiv: For the POC timeline — we need about two weeks to review compliance docs, then run the POC for a week. Can you support that schedule?
[10:49] Maya: Yes — we'll target sending docs tomorrow and propose POC in the week of 2027-09-27.
[10:57] Lina: Who's our point of contact for security questions during the POC?
[11:01] Maya: Lina, Diego will be the SE lead for POC and Maya for procurement and contract.
[11:06] Marcus: For acceptance criteria, we'll measure p95 latency under 350ms for typical prompt and no data leakage.
[11:15] Diego: Noted. We'll include those SLOs in the test plan.
[11:19] Rajiv: Any blockers from Redwood side for connecting to our VPC?
[11:24] Diego: Just the network whitelisting and PKI cert exchange for PrivateLink/peering; we'll provide the technical checklist.
[11:32] Maya: Quick recap — we'll send SOC2/ISO and pen test summary, Diego will send POC plan, Marcus will share network diagram, and we'll propose POC dates.
[11:42] Lina: Sounds good.
[11:45] Rajiv: Thanks all.
[11:48] Maya: Thanks, we'll follow up with docs and next steps.

End of meeting.

Notes on transcription: Minor speaker attribution errors and some words transcribed phonetically (e.g., K-V cash for KV cache).
